title: A Compass for the Clock
premise: In the final winter of the Republic of Vessany, Quentin Kavanagh carries sealed dispatches aboard the diplomatic packet ship Meridian, sworn to invisibility and to the codes sewn into their coat lining. But a census taker's probing questions in the port city of Callowmark expose them, forcing Quentin into the open world of dockworkers, exiles, and a found family at the Saltglass boarding house. There they discover that among the 'enemies' now declared by the collapsing republic is Ilse Marchetti, the translator to whom Quentin once promised safe passage in peacetime. To keep that promise before the Meridian sails on the morning tide, Quentin must choose between the duty encoded in their very name and the people who finally saw them — smuggling Ilse aboard under a dead man's papers while the census taker closes in. The book ends with the ship slipping out at dawn: Quentin burns the codes unread, stays behind on the quay with their chosen family, and mails a single honest letter to the republic that no longer exists.
about_author: Lior Oyelaran is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing the letters of undocumented port workers before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where the tide tables still dictate the rhythm of daily life.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In Vessany's dying capital, Quentin receives final orders, sews codes into their coat, and rehearses being nobody. Flashback seeds the peacetime promise made to Ilse Marchetti over tea and translation drafts. Emotional beat: the cold comfort of duty as armor against grief.

chapters.title: The Packet Ship Meridian
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Aboard the Meridian, Quentin maps the ship's rhythms and its small crew: Captain Oduya, stoker Fenwick, and the captain's ward, Tamsin. A storm forces Quentin to help in the galley, breaking their own rule of detachment. Emotional beat: the first crack in invisibility.

chapters.title: Callowmark Harbor
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The ship docks in neutral Callowmark for repairs; Quentin delivers dispatches to a consulate already burning its files. The city is full of refugees from the republic Quentin serves. Emotional beat: vertigo — serving a state that is visibly ending.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the harbor census office, taker Ambrose Pell asks not just names but loyalties, kinships, debts. Quentin lies well but notices Pell writing something extra in the margin. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root; the sense of being measured.

chapters.title: The Saltglass Boarding House
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, seeking cheap lodging during repairs. The boarding house run by Widow Sefu holds exiles, deserters, and a deaf clockmaker named Bram who mends timepieces no one claims. Quentin is taken in without being asked a single question. Emotional beat: warmth offered freely for the first time.

chapters.title: A Name on the Enemy List
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A posted proclamation lists persons barred from republican territory or protection; among them, Ilse Marchetti, translator, traitor by decree. Quentin learns she is living somewhere in Callowmark. Emotional beat: the promise resurfaces like a debt come due.

chapters.title: Bram's Clocks
chapters.summary: Bram's POV (rendered through gesture and written notes). The clockmaker observes Quentin searching the city each evening and begins leaving repaired watches on Quentin's pillow — gifts, or messages. Emotional beat: communication without interrogation; found family forming wordlessly.

chapters.title: The Translator's Lodging
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Following a trail of translated pamphlets, Quentin finds Ilse working under a false name in a print shop. Their reunion is wary — she believes Quentin may have come to arrest her. Emotional beat: love strained across the new border drawn between them.

chapters.title: Terms of an Old Promise
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse recounts her own fall: denounced by a colleague, stripped of position, hunted. She tests Quentin's loyalty with hard questions about what the dispatches contain. Quentin cannot answer honestly. Emotional beat: the cost of secrets inside intimacy.

chapters.title: Pell Makes His Rounds
chapters.summary: Ambrose Pell's POV. The census taker cross-references his margins, suspects the Saltglass house harbors undeclared persons, and requests naval assistance to inspect the Meridian's passenger manifest. Emotional beat: bureaucratic menace — evil as paperwork.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Papers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Fenwick reveals he carries identity documents of a stoker who died at sea, kept 'for emergencies.' Quentin must ask for them — spending another person's mercy. Emotional beat: guilt braided with hope.

chapters.title: The Consulate Burns
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Summoned to deliver the last dispatches, Quentin instead witnesses the consulate destroying records and staff fleeing. An official hints the Meridian will be searched at departure and that 'irregular passengers' will be shot as spies. Emotional beat: the machinery of the state turning openly predatory.

chapters.title: What the Codes Say
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, alone at night. Quentin nearly deciphers the sewn dispatches, suspecting they order the Meridian to abandon allies in Callowmark — possibly naming Ilse. Fear of knowing wars with need to know. Emotional beat: dread as a form of complicity.

chapters.title: Tamsin Asks Why
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The captain's ward, sharp-eyed, catches Quentin measuring the hold and forging a berth entry. Instead of reporting, she offers to help, revealing her own stowaway past. Emotional beat: solidarity between people shaped by hiding.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Tide
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The plan crystallizes: Ilse comes aboard as the dead stoker's cousin at first light. The Saltglass household gathers for a farewell supper that everyone pretends is ordinary. Bram gives Quentin a pocket compass that points not north but 'home,' whatever direction that is. Emotional beat: tenderness under countdown pressure.

chapters.title: Pell at the Gangway
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At dawn inspection, Pell boards the Meridian with the manifest. He interrogates 'the stoker's cousin' while Quentin stands by, one lie from ruin. Tamsin misdirects; Captain Oduya invokes maritime law. Pell retreats — but promises to return with soldiers. Emotional beat: terror held perfectly still.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Lines cast off; Ilse is aboard and safe. On the quay, the Saltglass family waves — and Quentin realizes they cannot board. The promise was never to leave together; it was that Ilse would get out. Emotional beat: heartbreak chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: Burning the Codes
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, watching the Meridian shrink. Quentin cuts the dispatches from their coat lining and feeds them to the harbor water, unread. The republic's last orders dissolve. Emotional beat: liberation indistinguishable from treason.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the post office, Quentin writes to the republic — a single page resigning, confessing, and testifying to what was done in its name. Addressed to an office likely already empty. Emotional beat: accountability when no one demands it.

chapters.title: Census, Amended
chapters.summary: Ambrose Pell's POV. Pell finds Quentin at the Saltglass house, warrant in hand — but finds a household vouching for one another, testimony he cannot easily file. Faced with Bram's clocks, Tamsin's defiance, and Quentin's open confession, Pell tears up the margin note. Emotional beat: a bureaucrat choosing humanity over procedure.

chapters.title: A Compass for the Clock
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Weeks later: Quentin works the print shop beside Ilse's old colleagues, learning a trade that puts words in public view. Letters arrive from Ilse via neutral ports. Bram sets the compass into a clock face on the mantel. Emotional beat: home rebuilt from chosen parts.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings Back
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating brief POVs — Sefu, Tamsin, Fenwick, finally Quentin. News comes that the republic has fallen; the Meridian reached safe harbor with Ilse aboard. On the quay at dusk, the Saltglass family watches ships come in, and Quentin understands that staying visible was the whole point. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
